# GENERATED -- do not edit by hand.
#
#   uv pip compile --generate-hashes --no-header --python-version 3.13 \
#       requirements.in -o requirements.txt
#
# DEPS ONLY -- spiderfoot itself is NOT in this file and cannot be. Upstream
# ships neither setup.py nor pyproject.toml, so pip cannot install it as a
# package at all ("tier C", see packages/metagoofil/debian/rules for the
# mechanism this package copies). dh_virtualenv builds the environment from
# these pins; debian/rules then fetches the upstream source tree separately,
# pinned by commit SHA in debian/upstream.pin, and lays it down beside the
# venv. The two pinning mechanisms are independent on purpose: PyPI artifact
# hashes here, a git content hash there.
#
# THE INPUTS ARE NOT UPSTREAM'S requirements.txt VERBATIM.
#
# This is the one package in this repo where that is true, and it is a
# deliberate, documented divergence rather than an oversight. Upstream pins a
# wall of 2023-era UPPER bounds that are largely uninstallable on trixie's
# Python 3.13 -- most importantly cryptography>=3.4.8,<4, which has no cp313
# wheel and would drag a Rust/cargo toolchain into the build. The upper bounds
# are therefore stripped and the lower bounds kept.
#
# TWO upper bounds are deliberately RETAINED, because relaxing them was tested
# and found to break upstream code at runtime, not at install time:
#
#   PyPDF2<2     3.0.0 removed PdfFileReader; modules/sfp_filemeta.py calls it
#   secure<0.4.0 1.0 removed .framework; sfwebui.py calls .framework.cherrypy()
#
# Both retained versions are pure Python and install cleanly on 3.13, so
# keeping them costs nothing. Do NOT "finish the job" by stripping these two
# as well -- the web UI will not start and PDF metadata extraction will break.
#
# debian/README.Debian carries the full table of every relaxed pin against its
# upstream original, with the shipped version and the reason. READ IT before
# regenerating this file: a regeneration straight from upstream's
# requirements.txt silently undoes all of this work.
#
# uv rather than pip-compile: --generate-hashes downloads every platform wheel
# of every pin in order to hash it, and pip-compile does that serially. With
# spiderfoot's dependency set -- 60 resolved packages from 26 direct
# requirements -- that does not finish in reasonable time.
#
# --require-hashes lives in this file rather than in an --extra-pip-arg,
# because dh_virtualenv would apply the flag to the unpinned pip/setuptools/
# wheel bootstrap as well and the build would fail before it started.
--require-hashes
